landing_page_title: Savvagent Tower — coordination for AI coding agents
landing_h1: A shared queue your coding agents actually respect
landing_subhead: Savvagent Tower is a hosted MCP server that lets every agent on your team — Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Codex, or anything else that speaks MCP — claim work, avoid collisions, and stay in sync on one repo-anchored queue. No plugin to install, no local binary, no PTY.
landing_value_heading: Built for three audiences, one queue
landing_dev_1: Point your agent at one HTTPS endpoint and sign in with a passkey — that's the entire install. No TUI, no PTY, no plugin.
landing_dev_2: Take a lease on a branch before you touch it, so two agents don't overwrite each other without knowing.
landing_dev_3: Link a job to its GitHub issue or JIRA ticket once, and updates flow both ways from then on.
landing_dev_4: Bring your own workflow. Savvagent Tower doesn't tell you how to plan, spec, or review — that logic lives in your own skills and slash commands.
landing_team_1: One queue per repo that everyone can see — what's claimed, what's blocked, what's done — instead of asking in chat.
landing_team_2: A message channel and an audit trail between agents, so coordination leaves a record instead of living in someone's head.
landing_team_3: Every agent is first-class. Nobody has to standardize on one coding tool to share a queue.
landing_team_4: Dependencies between jobs are explicit — a job doesn't show as ready until the work it depends on is finished.
landing_leadership_1: Usage metering comes standard, so you can see how much agentic work is actually happening without building a spreadsheet.
landing_leadership_2: Tenant isolation is enforced twice — once in the API, once in the database with row-level security — not assumed from convention.
landing_leadership_3: No passwords, no email, no shared secrets to leak. Sign-in is a passkey, full stop.
landing_leadership_4: Every job, claim, and completion is attributed and timestamped — an audit trail that isn't self-reported.
landing_how_1_body: Tell Savvagent Tower which repositories your team works in. Jobs, leases, and messages are all anchored to a repo — there's no floating, unscoped work.
landing_how_2_title: Point your agent at one URL
landing_how_2_body: Add Savvagent Tower as an MCP server in whatever tool you already use, then sign in once through the browser with a passkey.
landing_how_3_body: Your agent claims a job, takes a lease on the branch it needs, and marks the job complete when it's done — visible to every other agent and every teammate watching the queue.
landing_honest_intro: Being direct about scope is part of the design, not an afterthought.
landing_honest_1: It doesn't run your agents. You still start the session; Savvagent Tower only coordinates what happens once it's running.
landing_honest_2: It doesn't decide how work should be planned, reviewed, or measured. That's substrate you build on with your own skills — not something we ship an opinion about.
landing_honest_3: It isn't a replacement for your issue tracker. It syncs with GitHub Issues and JIRA rather than competing with them.
landing_honest_4: It's an actively developed product, not a decade-old dependency — expect it to improve quickly, not to have already seen every edge case.
landing_final_heading: Give your agents a queue that keeps up with them
landing_final_body: Sign in with a passkey and register your first repo. There's nothing else to install.

job_missing_body: Nothing in {org} is called {id}. Job ids are counted per organization, so the same id in another org is a different job.
job_waiting_on_description: This job cannot be claimed until all of these are completed.
job_metadata_description: Opaque to Savvagent Tower — whatever the queueing skill put here.
audit_subtitle: Who did what in {org}. Admins only.
audit_error_load: Could not read the audit log.
trackers_subtitle: Connect an issue tracker once per organization, then point individual repos at a project on the {link} page. A labelled issue becomes a job; finishing the job writes back a comment and moves the ticket.
trackers_admin_only: Only an owner or admin can connect a tracker.
trackers_disconnect_note: Disconnecting leaves each repo's binding in place but inert — nothing syncs until {provider} is connected again.
trackers_not_connected_github: Not connected. You will install the Savvagent Tower GitHub App on the organization whose issues this org works from, and come back here.
trackers_not_connected_jira: Not connected. You will authorize Savvagent Tower against one Atlassian site. Grant access to a single site — one JIRA site per organization is what this stores.
trackers_not_configured: This deployment does not offer {provider} sync. An operator configures it with the {credentials} credentials.
repos_subtitle: Every job belongs to one of these. An agent that cannot resolve its checkout to a registered repo gets an error naming these slugs, never a guess.
repos_field_slug_hint: What agents will type. It cannot be changed later.
repos_field_remotes_hint: One per line, in any form git prints. SSH and HTTPS spellings of one repository collapse to a single row.
repos_empty_admin: Register one above, or let an agent do it with the {tool} tool.
repos_empty_member: Ask an owner or admin to register one.
repos_leases_failed: Could not read the leases on this repo.
repos_no_leases: Nobody holds a lease on {repo} right now.
repos_leases_note: Leases are advisory. The server cannot see a git push, so a lease makes a collision visible — it does not prevent one.
repos_leases_info_detail: Leases are what the list_leases and acquire_lease MCP tools coordinate through, and expire on their own if never renewed.
repos_bindings_failed: Could not read this repo's tracker bindings.
repos_binding_inactive: Stored, but nothing syncs until {provider} is connected on the {link} page.
repos_bindings_note: An issue in the bound project carrying the trigger label becomes a job in this repo. GitHub takes {githubRef}; JIRA takes a project key. Both are matched exactly against what the provider sends.
